status: authored 2026-10-01, extended 2026-10-02. SIX sites measured off the canonical heightmap. THREE are SCHEDULED in data/placements.json (2026-10-02: the Crown Cemetery and the two Necrozma towers, each named by `scheduled_as`), because nothing they give depends on a right-click altar; their `placement` block was deleted here as placement_method.not_in_placements_json requires, and this file keeps the measurement and the reasoning. THREE stay sited and NOT scheduled (Mew, Zapdos, Articuno): each one's encounter is a right-click altar, and EXP-048 has not yet shown that a pasted altar answers. The two towers were re-homed from the End, which no player can enter. Of the eight Nether and End structures, the other six are re-opened one by one in the refused entry: the four Ruinous shrines STAY (their stakes generate only as Nether features), and Moltres and Eternatus have better homes only once the campaign supplies what their altars want.
why_a_sibling_of_legendaries_json: data/legendaries.json is OUR parametric chamber system, not a register of sites. tools/legendaries.py `load()` rejects any record whose `kind` is outside (lake_grotto, sealed_chamber, sapling_wake) and any record without a non-empty `gate.flags`, and `geometry()` derives every box of a sited record from `mouth`/`portal`, `approach` and `chamber`. A pasted third-party template has none of those: no bore, no shell margin, no carve, and - the load-bearing one - NO GATE WE MAY AUTHOR, because what triggers a `lumymon:*_altar` has never been read (LumyMon is closed source).

Putting these three in that file would therefore mean mutating KINDS and the gate rule of a generator that emits six built chambers, to carry records it must never emit. That is the opposite of fail-closed, so they live here.

No id and no species in this file is authored in data/legendaries.json: that file owns mesprit, azelf, uxie, regirock, regice, registeel, regigigas, groudon, lugia and celebi_wake; this one owns mew, calyrex (with spectrier), zapdos, articuno and necrozma (both towers). Checked 2026-10-01 - there is no two-author id and no two-author legendary. The three lakes were REFUSED for exactly that reason (see refused).

placement_method.proven: VERIFIED on THIS runtime (Minecraft 1.21.1, Fabric 0.19.5, Cobblemon 1.8.0, 2026-09-09): legendarymonuments:firescourge_shrine PASSED via raw `/place template`, with rotation 90 and mirror front_back both PASS (docs/world-building/STRUCTURE_WORKFLOW.md:81,90). 'Functional elements UNKNOWN' in the same record.
placement_method.anchor: `/place template` takes the structure's MINIMUM corner, so every `corner` below is the command's x/z and every `y` is the bottom layer. anchor_mode is therefore always `corner` and y_mode `absolute`.
placement_method.rotation_is_none_on_purpose: No .nbt has been read, so which way a template's door faces is UNKNOWN and a rotation chosen to 'face the approach' would be invented. Each site records `rotation: none` as the command form AND the measured ground for the transposed footprint, so 90 or 270 remains free at no cost once someone has looked at the paste. Mirror stays `none`.
placement_method.not_in_placements_json: Deliberate, and it is the id-authorship rule: until a paste is approved these three ids have ONE author, this file. Whoever schedules one copies template, cell, position (x, y, z), size, rotation, mirror, anchor_mode `corner`, y_mode `absolute` and a `source.licence` line into a data/placements.json `kind: donor` record, and then DELETES the `placement` block here, leaving the measurement and the reasoning. Two files carrying a position for the same site is the invisible collision data/id_authorship.json exists to catch.

what_is_actually_known: CORRECTED 2026-10-02 (docs/research/notes/legendary-catalogue-reopened.md section 6). This line said Mew's command blocks gate on Cobbleverse's `defeat_champion_blue` 'which our progression NEVER GRANTS', so the chain was 'inert by construction'. The read does not support that: the advancement is granted by `rctmod:defeat_count` on `kanto_champion_blue`, OUR Champion is `kanto_champion_blue` (data/league_trainers.json:125, data/progression.json champion_cleared), and data/progression.json upstream_neutralised empties its reward function precisely so 'the advancement grants cleanly'. So it is very probably granted on beating our Blue (INFERRED, not seen in game). Mew's door is inert today only because enable-command-block is false.
VERIFIED: the Necrozma towers (not adopted) run `pokespawnat ... level=80` from command blocks, so command blocks in these templates do carry working commands.

SHAPE NOW VERIFIED, 2026-10-02, from the LumyMon-0.6.6 jar's class strings and lang (no decompiling; docs/research/notes/lumymon-altars.md): each altar is a plain block, NOT a block entity, and fires on an item in hand - articuno_altar on a glacier_feather, zapdos_altar on a thunder_feather, mew_shrine on an origin_fossil, calyrex_statue on a calyrex_crown - while summon_trigger reacts to an item ENTITY (shaderoot or iceroot carrot). WHERE THE ITEMS COME FROM, measured 2026-10-02 against the server's own files: the feathers and the crown are NOT in the templates. Articuno's only barrel holds wind charges, ice gems, glass panes, breeze rods and diamond boots; Zapdos's holds redstone, electric gems, a trident and copper bulbs; the cemetery has no stocked barrel. Across all 102 mod jars and every server datapack, NO recipe or loot table produces a glacier_feather, thunder_feather or calyrex_crown - they appear only as advancement icons and as TM-recipe ingredients - so a player has no data-defined way to get them (a drop coded inside a mod is not excluded). The two exceptions: the origin_fossil has a LumyMon recipe, and the shaderoot carrot drops from the crop the cemetery template pastes fully grown, so the Spectrier route at the cemetery is self-contained. STILL UNVERIFIED: whether an altar needs a summon_anchor nearby (none of the Articuno, Zapdos or Mew templates contains one, so that is the likeliest failure) and whether the item is consumed. The earlier claim of 'level 70-90' was relayed from STRUCTURE_DECISIONS.md:216-217, uncited, and is WRONG for the birds; see and_the_level_problem.
UNKNOWN: whether an altar needs state written at WORLDGEN time rather than at placement. If it does, a pasted altar is scenery for ever.
a_dead_altar_must_not_block.and_the_level_problem: If an altar ever does summon, data/level_cap.json applies: a Pokemon strictly above the thrower's RCT level cap breaks free from every ball, a Master Ball included. The levels, VERIFIED from the jar's pokespawnat strings: Articuno and Zapdos 50-60, Mew 75-90, Calyrex 70, Spectrier 50-59. So the earlier conclusion - that a working altar would 'most likely produce an UNCATCHABLE legendary' - holds for Mew and Calyrex, which are above the 65 upper bound at champion, and does NOT hold for the two birds, which are catchable once a player's cap reaches the level rolled. Which badge that is, and whether a 50-60 bird at Frostpeak and the windward skerries fits the curve, is a question for trainer-balance-designer, not for this file. Nothing may still depend on an altar working.

spectrier_once_per_player.status: DESIGNED, NOT BUILT. The cemetery may be placed without it: until it lands, Spectrier stays repeatable.
spectrier_once_per_player.why_lumymon_cannot_do_it: the trigger's only brakes are a 'pokemon_already_nearby' check and a cooldown held in an in-memory map keyed by player UUID (lumymon-altars.md section 1), lost on restart. LumyMon is closed source; nothing in its config (11 keys) caps a summon.
mechanism: a tick function guarded by `execute if entity @a[<within 32 of the trigger ring (4153, 112, 1999)>]`, so it costs nothing when nobody is there
ATTRIBUTE: each tick, a lumymon:shaderoot_carrot item entity within 4 of the ring has its `Thrower` UUID copied to storage cobblers:spectrier last_thrower

RECORD: when a wild cobblemon:pokemon of species spectrier, untagged, appears within 16 of the anchor (4153, 112, 1999), tag it and grant cobblers:legendary/spectrier_summoned to the player whose UUID is last_thrower (a macro: `$advancement grant @a[nbt={UUID:$(u)}] only ...`). An advancement is per player and permanent, which is exactly the cap asked for.

REFUSE: each tick, for every player holding that advancement within 32, a macro kills any shaderoot carrot item entity within 4 of the ring whose Thrower is that player, before the trigger can take it. The carrot is lost; a tellraw says why.
weak_points: a carrot thrown by player A and spawning Spectrier is credited to A, but a carrot that the trigger takes in the same tick it lands may never be seen by a 1-tick poll: EXP needed
a capped player can hand a carrot to an uncapped friend, who throws it: that is the friend's one Spectrier, which is the rule working, not a leak
UNVERIFIED that a player-thrown carrot fires the trigger at all (EXP-048 owner half, step 1). Build only after that answers.

refused.why: WE ALREADY AUTHOR ALL THREE. data/legendaries.json carries `uxie`, `azelf` and `mesprit` as lake grottos, three of them sited and emitted, and tools/legendaries.py builds their chambers and their badge gates. refused.and_also: all three are depth-7 jigsaws that generate NOWHERE in our install (their biome tag is in the disabled Sinnoh pack), so a raw paste yields one 37x48x37 start piece and no assembly.

refused.why: 120x90x137 is a region, not a structure - it would redraw whatever terrain it landed on - and it ships two SINNOH RCT trainers (`sinnoh_buck`, `team_galactic_charon`, data/structures.json:6480-6483) who have no place in a Kanto-series campaign. Its RCT spawners DO work in a pasted build (VERIFIED, EXP-013 E), which is what makes importing the wrong characters a real risk rather than a cosmetic one.

the island generates only inside Legendary Monuments' own Distortion World dimension. Adopting it means adopting a dimension, and dimensions are a world-critical dependency decision (CLAUDE.md principles 9 and 10), not a placement.

it ends at Calyrex, and so does `crown_cemetery`, which is adopted above. Two sites for one legendary is the checklist feeling the design is trying to avoid. If the owner prefers the spire (41x38x49, snowy_plains), it REPLACES the cemetery; it does not join it.

LEAVE THEM WHERE THEY ARE. The Nether and the End are vanilla-generated, so these keep their structure data, their terrain validation, their spacing and - the part a paste destroys - their finders. Already decided (STRUCTURE_INVENTORY.md:140-141, :320-321; DIMENSIONS_AND_BORDERS.md:317). Pasting one would be a strict downgrade. (Re-opened 2026-10-02: see reopened_2026_10_02.)

The stakes exist only because the Nether generates normally; a shrine pasted into our exported overworld would have no stakes anywhere.
